A SYNTHETIC MONTH

The decisions behind the balance

Start with $150 billed Pay In Full and $900 Pay Over Time. The shared revolving capacity is $1,000. On day 5, a $250 purchase arrives; on day 10, a $400 payment is received against a prior $190 minimum. At closing, eligible Pay In Full amounts are considered for transfer.

Calculated account principal and balance classification. Interest is displayed separately. At close, a transfer changes the buckets without changing total principal. Dates and amounts are synthetic.

WHAT THE DOCUMENTS ESTABLISH

Evidence, assumptions and missing inputs

Source statement review stays private. Its line items and closing balance were checked locally. Real balances, merchant history, source PDFs and identifiers are not served by this site.
  • Uploaded terms describe separate balance groups, shared Pay Over Time capacity and future effective-date changes.
  • The statement establishes a reported outcome. A zero-interest cycle alone cannot validate compounding or grace eligibility.
  • The public reference provides more detailed minimum, allocation and interest formulas. Confirm the actual account agreement and amendments before treating them as that account’s rules.
  • The daily calculation uses rounded DPR and exact rational compounding. Final half-up cent rounding and equal-APR ordering are modeling conventions to validate against issuer results.
  • Missing grace evidence produces an unknown interest result. No default APR, assumed zero interest or fabricated posting date fills the gap.
  • This standard-account example excludes cash/plan activity, payment programs, disputes, penalty assessment and benefit eligibility. Other functions have bounded tests; they are not a complete product implementation.
